tagline: Up the Rappahannock from one old tobacco port to another.
intro: Tidewater Trail leaves downtown Tappahannock as a divided highway along the west bank of the Rappahannock, crosses Mount Landing Creek and turns inland through Caret, Champlain, Chance and Loretto. Over Portobogo Creek it enters Caroline County and comes to Port Royal, an old port at the head of the river's sea-going reach.
Past Port Royal it runs as a two-lane road along the eastern edge of Fort A.P. Hill, through Rappahannock Academy, named for a military school that is gone, and on to the Spotsylvania line.

moments.title: Tappahannock
moments.text: The county seat began as Hobbs Hole, after a captain who anchored his ship in a deep spot of the river, and a British naval force burned its courthouse in 1814.

moments.title: Vauter's Church
moments.text: A T-shaped brick church from 1719 at Loretto, the upper church of St. Anne's Parish, which grew its south wing in 1731.

moments.title: Port Royal
moments.text: A tobacco port from 1652 whose last scheduled passenger ship left in 1932, and two miles out of town John Wilkes Booth was cornered in a tobacco barn.
